<thinking>
Root: एध् (edh), bhvadi, ātmanepada (anudātta ṭ... the ॒ marks anudātta → ātmanepada).

Lat, ātmanepada, 3rd sing: ta → te. Stem: एध + अ (śap) = एध. Guna of ए? ए is already... एध् has ए, guṇa-grade already. So एधते.
</thinking>

<answer>एधते</answer>

<thinking>
Root: एध् (edh), bhvadi, ātmanepada (anudātta ṭ... actually the marker is ॒ indicating anudātta → ātmanepada). Meaning: vṛddhau (to grow).

Lit (perfect): एध् begins with vowel 'ए' — roots beginning with vowels other than a, and having... For लिट्, roots beginning with a vowel that is not short 'a'? Rule: आम् प्रत्ययवत् — "इजादेश्च गुरुमतोऽनृच्छः" (3.1.36) requires आम् for roots beginning with a vowel (ijādi) that are gurumat (having a heavy vowel) and polysyllabic... Actually 3.1.35 कास्प्रत्ययादाममन्त्रे लिटि; 3.1.36 इजादेश्च गुरुमतोऽनृच्छः — a root beginning with a vowel (other than 'a'? "ijādi" = beginning with vowel of इच् i.e. any vowel except अ) and containing a guru vowel takes आम् in liṭ.

एध् — begins with ए (an इच्), and the vowel ए is guru (long). So it takes आम्: एधाम् + आस/बभूव/चकार. Standard: एधाञ्चक्रे, एधामास (āmāsa), एधाम्बभूव.

Since it's ātmanepada, auxiliary would be चक्रे (kṛ in ātmanepada) or आस/बभूव? आस् and भू are parasmaipada only. So ātmanepada uses चक्रे. So एधाञ्चक्रे.

But here it's bhāve prayoga (impersonal), which uses ātmanepada endings, third person singular normally. But required: madhyama purusha, eka vacana. In bhāve prayoga, the verb is always third person singular... but the exercise apparently wants madhyama ekavacana form anyway: liṭ ātmanepada madhyama eka = से → थास् → liṭ: थास् replaced by से (2nd sg ātmanepada liṭ = से). Yes, liṭ ātmanepada: ए, आते, इरे; से, आथे, ध्वे; ए, वहे, महे.

So with कृ: चकृषे. So एधाञ्चकृषे.

Bhāve prayoga: root takes यक्? No—bhāve/karmani prayoga in liṭ: sārvadhātuka? Actually यक् (3.1.67) applies for sārvadhātuka; liṭ endings are ārdhadhātuka, so no यक्. In liṭ karmaṇi/bhāve, forms are same as ātmanepada perfect. So एधाञ्चकृषे.

Hmm, but with आम् + auxiliary — in bhāve, auxiliary कृ in ātmanepada: चकृषे. Combined: एधाञ्चकृषे.

Alternatively एधाम्बभूविषे? No, bhū is parasmaipada.

Answer: एधाञ्चकृषे.</thinking><answer>एधाञ्चकृषे</answer>

<thinking>
Root: एध् (edh), bhvādi, ātmanepada (anudātta ṭit... actually एधँ॒ has anudātta indicating ātmanepada). Meaning "to grow/prosper".

Lit (perfect) of एध्: since it begins with a vowel (e), and is anekāc... एध् is a root beginning with a vowel, ending... Rule: आम् प्रत्यय (लिट् आम् for roots beginning with vowel and being anekāc) — कास्प्रत्ययादाममन्त्रे लिटि (3.1.35): कास् and pratyayas and ām... Actually 3.1.35: कास्प्रत्ययादाममन्त्रे लिटि. 3.1.36: इजादेश्च गुरुमतोऽनृच्छः — "ijādi roots with guru vowel (other than ṛch) take ām". एध् — begins with ए which is ijādi (starts with vowel other than a? "इजादि" = beginning with ij = vowels except a... actually इच् = vowels except अ). ए is इच्. And गुरुमत् — has a guru vowel (ए is guru, being dīrgha). So एध् takes आम्: एधाम् + कृ/भू/अस् liṭ.

So एधाञ्चक्रे (ātmanepada with कृ). Bhāve prayoga — impersonal, uses ātmanepada endings, always third person singular normally. But here madhyama puruṣa ekavacana is asked... In bhāva prayoga, verb is always prathama puruṣa ekavacana. But these tasks sometimes ask forms anyway — the form generated with madhyama ekavacana ending.

Ātmanepada liṭ madhyama ekavacana ending: थास् → से. With आम् + कृ: एधाञ्चकृषे.

Let's check: कृ in liṭ ātmanepada: चक्रे, चकृषे, चकृढ्वे... madhyama singular चकृषे. So एधाञ्चकृषे.

Alternatively with भू: एधांबभूविषे? No, भू is parasmaipada. अस्: आस? आस is parasmaipada too. So कृ ātmanepada: एधाञ्चकृषे.

But bhāve prayoga uses ātmanepada endings. Yes. So answer: एधाञ्चकृषे.

Sandhi: आम् + चकृषे → आञ्चकृषे (anusvāra → ñ before c). Written एधाञ्चकृषे or एधाञ्चकृषे.

Hmm, but wait — bhāve prayoga of intransitive root: karmani/bhave passive requires यक् in sārvadhātuka; in liṭ (ārdhadhātuka), passive uses ātmanepada endings without yak, with... actually for liṭ, kartari vs bhāve differ only in endings being ātmanepada. So एधाञ्चकृषे is the answer? But for bhāve, the form should be... For roots that are already ātmanepada in kartari, the bhāve form is identical. Yes.

Actually, there's a rule: in ārdhadhātuka lakāras for karmaṇi/bhāve, some prescribe using cin/... no. Standard: liṭ karmaṇi uses ātmanepada endings with the same stem.

Answer: एधाञ्चकृषे</thinking><answer>एधाञ्चकृषे</answer>

<thinking>
Bhave prayoga uses atmanepada endings, and is always third person singular. But the task asks for uttama purusha bahuvacana — in such artificial paradigms (as in tables of bhāva prayoga), forms are generated with all endings anyway. Actually many textbooks give bhāve prayoga forms only in prathama-purusha ekavacana. But some exercise sets generate full paradigms mechanically using ātmanepada endings.

So Lit ātmanepada of भू: बभूवे, बभूविषे... Actually लिट् of भू ātmanepada: बभूवे, बभूविषे, बभूविध्वे... uttama bahuvacana ending is "महिङ्" → महे. With iṭ: बभूविमहे.

Let's check: भू in liṭ ātmanepada: बभूवे (1s), बभूविषे (2s), बभूवे (3s)? Standard: liṭ ātmanepada endings: ए, आते, इरे; से, आथे, ध्वे; ए, वहे, महे.

Root भू + liṭ: reduplication बभू. Before vowel endings, ऊ → उव् (uvaṅ? actually भू + ए → बभूवे via "अचि श्नुधातुभ्रुवां य्वोरियङुवङौ" → बभुव् + ए = बभूवे? Actually ऊ→ उव, giving बभुवे. Hmm, standard form is बभूव for parasmaipada 3s (vṛddhi/guṇa). For ātmanepada: बभूवे — yes with वुक् augment (भुवो वुग्लुङिलिटोः) — "भुवो वुग्लुङ्लिटोः" gives भू + वुक् → भूव्. So बभूव् + ए = बभूवे.

For consonant endings with iṭ: बभूव् + इ + महे = बभूविमहे. Wait, does vuk apply before consonant endings? Sutra: भुवो वुग्लुङ्लिटोः — vuk augment for भू in luṅ and liṭ. Applies to the aṅga before ārdhadhātuka? Traditionally forms: बभूव, बभूविथ, बभूविम... yes बभूविम (uttama plural parasmaipada). So ātmanepada बभूविमहे.
</thinking>

<answer>बभूविमहे</answer>

<thinking>
Root: एध् (edh), bhvadi, ātmanepada (anudātta ṅit — it's marked ॒ indicating ātmanepada).

Lat, ātmanepada, 3rd sg: ते ending → एधते.

Stem: एध् + शप् (a) → एध + ते = एधते.
</thinking>

<answer>एधते</answer>

<thinking>
Bhave prayoga uses atmanepada endings, and the verb is always third person singular... but here the required is uttama purusha bahuvacana. In bhave prayoga, strictly the verb is always prathama purusha ekavacana. However, these exercise datasets often just generate the atmanepada form for the given person/number.

So we need Lit atmanepada uttama purusha bahuvacana of भू.

भू in Lit: बभूव. Atmanepada forms: बभूवे, बभूविषे... Actually भू takes परस्मैपद only, but in bhave/karmani it takes atmanepada endings.

Lit atmanepada of भू: root बभूव- with भू + आम्? Actually भू in Lit uses "बभूव" with the augment व् (भुवो वुग्लुङिलिटोः - vuk augment before ajadi ardhadhatuka). Rule 6.4.88: भुवो वुग्लुङ्लिटोः — भू gets वुक् augment in luṅ and liṭ. So बभूव् + endings.

Atmanepada Lit endings: ए, आते, इरे; से, आथे, ध्वे; ए, वहे, महे.

Uttama bahuvacana: महे → with iṭ? Lit ardhadhatuka; महे is a kit? For liṭ, the sārvadhātuka... liṭ endings are ārdhadhātuka-like for set/it augment: iṭ is added to liṭ endings that are valādi (7.2.13 kṛsṛbhṛvṛstudru... niyama for it). Actually rule 7.2.35 आर्धधातुकस्येड् वलादेः gives iṭ before valādi ārdhadhātuka. महे begins with म् which is val. So iṭ: इमहे.

So बभूव् + इमहे = बभूविमहे.

Hmm, check: बभूविथ (2nd sg parasmaipada) — yes, बभूविथ. Similarly बभूविमहे? Actually parasmaipada uttama bahuvacana: बभूविम. So atmanepada: बभूविमहे.

Wait — but is the vuk augment added before iṭ-initial endings? Rule 6.4.88 भुवो वुग्लुङ्लिटोः applies to भू before luṅ and liṭ affixes, ajādi condition? The rule follows "अचि श्नुधातुभ्रुवां..."? Actually 6.4.88 is in the section; वुक् is added when the affix is... बभूव, बभूविथ, बभूविम — all have व्. Yes, बभूविथ is standard. So बभूविमहे.
</thinking>

<answer>बभूविमहे</answer>
